IGUI_AutoPilot_E_NewTemplate: # Write your macro here. Example: <LINE> # while possible: <LINE> #     repair("Base.BaseballBat", using="Base.DuctTape") <LINE> # A block: the lines indented by 4 spaces under a line ending with a colon.
IGUI_AutoPilot_E_Info: A macro does game actions, one at a time, as you would do them by hand. It is written in English, like Python. <LINE> Record: do the recipes by hand, then Finish: the macro writes itself. <LINE> Actions: craft("recipe", using="item", times=3), dismantle("item"), exercise("pushups", minutes=10), rest(), eat(), drink(), refill(), smoke(), wait(5), stop_if(...), stop(). <LINE> Work: repair("item", using="material"), sharpen("item"), read("book"); conditions xp_gained("Maintenance") >= 100, condition("item") < 15, has("item", damaged=True), dark, hour >= 20, known("recipe"). A repair or a sharpening counts when the game gives experience or changes the item. <LINE> Workbenches (if the admin turns them on): craft("recipe", at="bench"), smelt("item", at="Primitive_Furnace"), sharpen("item", at="Grindstone"), condition bench_free("bench"). The character walks to the nearest bench and uses it as by hand; if another player is using it, it waits 30 seconds, then stops. <LINE> Items and places (if the admin turns them on): take("item", from="place", n=10), put("item", into="place"), put("made", into="place") (what the macro made), drop("item"), equip("item"), walk_to("place"); conditions count("item", at="place"), space_left(). A place is a crate or a square: write its name, then Insert > Items and places > Mark and click it. Never favourite, held or worn items; locked crates and other people's safehouses stay closed. <LINE> Blocks: repeat 10:, while possible:, while skill("Maintenance") < 4:, while True:, if ...: / elif ...: / else:. The block is the lines under it, indented by 4 spaces: no end. <LINE> when hungry: eat() - the when blocks are checked only in the pauses, never during an action, and hold for the whole macro. <LINE> Food and water: eat() eats what you carry or what is within reach (fridge, furniture, the floor next to you), never rotten, raw to cook, frozen or known poisonous, and opens the cans with a can opener; eat(near=False) only what you carry. drink(source=True) drinks at a sink or a barrel with clean water, refill() fills the bottles; conditions has_food(), has_drink(). <LINE> Conditions: has("item", at_least=20), count("item") >= 3, skill("Maintenance") < 4, hungry, thirsty, craving, tired... alone: when the game shows them; with a number the level, hungry >= 2 (Insert > Condition; hover the word), with and, or, not. <LINE> It stops like every job: move, zombies, severe thirst... and always says why. Favourite items are never used. <LINE> While you type, a list under the cursor shows what can be written there: arrows to choose, Enter or Tab to insert, Esc to close, Ctrl+Space to open it (option "Macro editor: typing suggestions"). <LINE> Enter starts the new line at the right indentation, Tab and Shift+Tab move the line, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes, Ctrl+D duplicates the line, Ctrl+/ comments it (option "Macro editor: auto indentation"). The mouse resting on a word says what it does and, on a state, its levels (option "Macro editor: hover help"). Native name: press it and click an object, in the inventory or in the world, for the game's name a macro writes. <LINE> With a controller: record and run; writing needs the keyboard. Limits: the admin sets them.

IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex5_Text: # Push-ups up to Strength 5 (push-ups train Strength, squats and sit-ups Fitness). <LINE> # In the pauses, never during an exercise: eat and drink what you carry or what is within reach (it opens the cans), smoke, rest on the nearest chair. <LINE> # A moodle alone holds when the game shows it; exerted >= 3: too tired for the exercises. <LINE> when hungry: <LINE>     eat() <LINE> when thirsty: <LINE>     drink() <LINE> when craving: <LINE>     smoke() <LINE> when exerted >= 3: <LINE>     rest(seat="nearest") <LINE> while skill("Strength") < 5: <LINE>     exercise("pushups", minutes=10)
IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex1_Text: # Maintenance: repair the damaged bats in your bag with duct tape <LINE> # (a table nearby is needed). Mark the bat you really use as favourite: <LINE> # the macro never touches it. A repair the game fails still counts. <LINE> while has("Base.BaseballBat", damaged=True) and has("Base.DuctTape"): <LINE>     stop_if(skill("Maintenance") >= 3) <LINE>     repair("Base.BaseballBat", using="Base.DuctTape")
IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex2_Text: # Carving up to level 3 from tree branches: stakes at level 0, <LINE> # sticks at 1, medium handles at 2 (these with a table nearby). <LINE> # It stops before the knife is ruined: write yours in condition(). <LINE> when exerted >= 3: <LINE>     rest(seat="nearest") <LINE> while skill("Carving") < 3: <LINE>     stop_if(condition("Base.KitchenKnife") < 15) <LINE>     if skill("Carving") < 1: <LINE>         craft("MakeStake", using="Base.TreeBranch2") <LINE>     elif skill("Carving") < 2: <LINE>         craft("CarveStick", using="Base.TreeBranch2") <LINE>     else: <LINE>         craft("CarveMediumHandle", using="Base.TreeBranch2")
IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex3_Text: # Electronics: dismantle the small devices (CD players, remotes, <LINE> # alarms, speakers) while you have them. A screwdriver is needed. <LINE> while possible: <LINE>     craft("DismantleMiscElectronics")
IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex4_Text: # The book first: "Maintenance I" makes the first levels go up faster. <LINE> # Then sharpen the kitchen knives with the whetstone while you can, <LINE> # only with light and before 22 (the game's hour). <LINE> read("Base.BookMaintenance1") <LINE> while possible: <LINE>     stop_if(dark or hour >= 22) <LINE>     sharpen("Base.KitchenKnife")

IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex6_Text: # Blacksmithing from 0 to 3: melt the crude blade, make the quarter bar, forge the blade, again. <LINE> # Needs: a hammer, tongs, an empty crucible, a crude blade (or a quarter bar) to start; <LINE> # a primitive furnace and a primitive forge nearby (or their bigger sisters). <LINE> # The charcoal (3 a round) comes from the crate "Charcoal": Duplicate, then Insert > Items and places. <LINE> when exerted >= 3: <LINE>     rest(seat="nearest") <LINE> when thirsty: <LINE>     drink() <LINE> if has("Base.BookBlacksmith1"): <LINE>     read("Base.BookBlacksmith1") <LINE> while skill("Blacksmith") < 3: <LINE>     stop_if(dark) <LINE>     if count("Base.Charcoal") < 3: <LINE>         take("Base.Charcoal", from="Charcoal", n=15) <LINE>     if has("Base.CrudeBlade"): <LINE>         smelt("Base.CrudeBlade", at="Primitive_Furnace") <LINE>     if has("Base.IronChunk"): <LINE>         craft("Forge_Bar_Quarter_From_Chunk", at="Forge_Primitive_Forge") <LINE>     craft("Forge_Crude_Blade", at="Forge_Primitive_Forge")

IGUI_AutoPilot_MA_Ex7_Text: # Electrical with crates: takes the remotes from "Radio crate", dismantles them, <LINE> # puts the parts into "Parts crate" when the backpack is heavy. Needs a screwdriver. <LINE> # First mark the two places: Duplicate, then Insert > Items and places. <LINE> while count("Base.Remote", at="Radio crate") > 0 or has("Base.Remote"): <LINE>     if not has("Base.Remote"): <LINE>         take("Base.Remote", from="Radio crate", n=5) <LINE>     dismantle("Base.Remote") <LINE>     if space_left() < 2: <LINE>         put("made", into="Parts crate") <LINE> put("made", into="Parts crate")

IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_MacroAutoIndent_Toolti: On a new line the cursor goes to the right indentation by itself: one level more after a colon, one less after break, pass and stop(). else and elif go back to their if; Backspace in the indentation goes back one level; Tab and Shift+Tab move the line; ( and " close by themselves. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes, Ctrl+D duplicates the line, Ctrl+/ (or Ctrl+Shift+7) comments it out, Ctrl+Enter checks the macro, Home goes to the first character. Off: the keys do what they always did.

IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_Notify_Tooltip: ZomBOT writes to you privately on Discord when an AutoPilot job starts, has a problem or ends, with the buttons Stop and Logout. Before the first message the game asks you once to confirm who they go to. Off (the default): nothing.

IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_NotifyEarly_Tooltip: Before the job stops: zombies in sight, hunger or thirst rising, a tool about to break, a nearly full inventory, darkness. Wounds, bites, bleeding and fire always come.
IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_NotifyRest: Also tell me about rest breaks
IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_NotifyRest_Tooltip: Off (the default): short breaks send nothing. A break longer than 5 minutes always comes.
IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_NotifyManual: Also tell me when I stop it myself
IGUI_AutoPilot_MO_NotifyManual_Tooltip: A short message, without Stop, when the job stops because you moved or pressed Stop.
